Notes for agents

Source: AGENTS.md

Scope

parvenu is a collection of fast, multithreaded utilities for large vectors, with no R package dependencies, in two families:

  • Base R functions that give base R’s results, named par_ plus the base name. Results identical to base are the promise, and tests compare against base.
  • Text search with Rust’s regex and aho-corasick crates, named par_ plus a stringr verb for one regex (par_detect()), and with _term for many terms at once (par_match_term()). These can’t give base’s results, since the syntax is Rust’s, so their docs say where they differ.

The text family is where threads pay off most: search is bound by the CPU, where hashing numbers is bound by memory and collapse is already close to that limit. Building R strings happens on R’s thread only, so functions that return new strings gain less than those that return positions or counts.

A function belongs here if it is useful in itself and clearly beats base. It doesn’t need to beat collapse, stringi, or other packages by a wide margin: if they tie or narrowly win, the function is still worth having. Cover every common use within a family, so users of one family don’t need another package for the rest of it. Don’t remove a function for a thin margin over other packages.

A simple R version is fine where it is good enough; Rust is for where it pays off. Measure against the fastest packages and report the numbers honestly, but don’t let them veto a good function.

markdown/PLAN.md

markdown/PLAN.md is a working record, not a set of rules. Much of it was written before any parvenu function, so it doesn’t always reflect how fast the package is. Revise it when it stands in the way of a good feature, rather than following it to the letter.

Formatting

Before every commit, run air format R/ tests/ and, in src/rust, cargo fmt. The pre-commit hook rejects staged R files that air would change. air.toml leaves test_that() blocks alone, so a test can keep a linear pipe flow on one line.

README figures

README plots are not committed to main, so re-knitting doesn’t add figures to the history. After knitting, replace the figures branch with a single commit, using the recipe in the setup chunk of README.Rmd. Don’t commit the README plots (man/figures/README-*) to main, and don’t keep a history on figures. The logo in man/figures/ does belong on main.

CI status

CI passed on all four jobs at 120d1c1 (2026-11-19), on R 4.6.2 as “release” and Rust 1.100 as “stable”. R 4.6.2 changed how strptime() reads seconds, which only CI caught, since R 4.5 is installed locally. Rust 1.100’s std calls WaitOnAddress on Windows, so src/Makevars.win.in links -lsynchronization; a new Rust can need another library there, which shows as “undefined reference” in 00install.out. Linux and Windows differ from macOS in ways local tests miss, so check each job after a push with gh run view <id>.
